card.name: Linking words before a condition term
card.fires_on: Small linking words such as "these" and "of" that come right before a disease or condition name in label text. The strongest case is "treat these" before "medical conditions".

modes.label: these before conditions
modes.description: The word "these" after "used to treat" in the NSAID cardiovascular warning.
modes.example: Use of ibuprofen may blunt the CV effects of several therapeutic agents used to treat<< these>> medical conditions (e.g., diure

modes.label: of after risk or evidence
modes.description: The word "of" in phrases like "risk of" or "no evidence of" before an outcome.
modes.example: therefore increasing the risk<< of>> breakthrough seizures.

modes.label: other list or filler words
modes.description: Bullets, "e.g.," or "been" in mid-sentence, where a condition term comes next.
modes.example: serious hypersensitivity reactions (e.g<<.,>> anaphylactic reactions and angio

card.writes: It pushes down disease and infection words (in English and Chinese) as the next word.
card.plain: It fires on small linking words just before a disease or condition is named, and it makes a disease word less likely to come next.
